passages.provision_quote: (b) A governmental entity may substantially burden a person's exercise of religion only if the governmental entity demonstrates that application of the burden to the person: (1) is in furtherance of a compelling governmental interest; and (2) is the least restrictive means of furthering that compelling governmental interest.
passages.note: Enrolled text: a strict-scrutiny RFRA (annex: rung 4); voting against it rules out the exemption side but does not seat rung 1, 2 or 3.
Bill details page (digest, sponsors); Pierce is not an author or sponsor, so it only identifies the instrument he voted against.
Forum remarks on LGBTQ politics, marriage equality and gender-affirming care name no rule on religious exemptions from anti-discrimination law.

rows.reasoning: Pierce voted Nay on SB 101 (2015), Indiana's Religious Freedom Restoration Act, which bars a governmental entity from substantially burdening religious exercise unless it is the least restrictive means of furthering a compelling interest; that places him against the rung to "allow faith-based exemptions from laws that conflict with sincere religious beliefs". A No vote does not show whether he would "prohibit religious exemptions", keep exemptions while ensuring religion "doesn't override anti-discrimination protections in employment and housing", or "balance" the two, so only a side is evidenced.
